parole.testo: Ultimately from Persian بالاخانه (bâlâxâne, “upper room”), via a Turkic language. Doublet of балахана (balaxana).

parole.significato: sarafan (a traditional long, trapeze-shaped Russian pinafore worn by women and girls)
parole.testo: Ultimately from Persian سراپا (sarâpâ, “from head to foot; honourable/honorable clothing”) via Turkic särapa(i) or Ancient Greek σάραπις (sárapis).

parole.significato: attic, garret, loft (an attic or similar space)
parole.testo: Attested since 16th century. From Persian چارتاق (čârtâq, “four-arch”) via a Turkic language. Possibly a doublet of чертог (čertog). Compare Turkish çardak, Azerbaijani чардаг / çardaq, Karakalpak шердақ (šerdaq), шертек (šertek), Crimean Tatar çardak, Karaim čardak.
